process_isolation.policy: Every executable input was launched as a separate direct child of the fresh audit runner. No timeout, Stop-Process, taskkill, signal, or intervention outside the auditor-owned process tree was used.

scientific_integrity.detail: All numerical claims are traceable to fresh stdout files or pinned source.

practice_boundaries.detail: The regulated Phase II request is routed to clinical-biostatistics/power-and-sample-size.

methodological_ground.detail: Independent realized-FDR assessment: the freshly executed shipped rnaseq_power.R printed nominal FDR 0.05 but Actual FDR 0.3692738, 0.1849111, 0.1024990, and 0.0598908 at 3, 5, 8, and 12 replicates. SKILL.md calls summaryPower/plotPower a target-FDR power curve but contains no rule to inspect Actual FDR, reject a failed candidate, increase simulations, or revise the model. The fresh pseudobulk run independently reinforces the gap: its 12-donor configuration reports FDR 0.133. A nominal alpha is a test setting, not evidence that realized FDR is controlled.

code_usability.detail: Both shipped R examples, package parsing, all six other computational inputs, and determinism completed with exit 0 in the designated environment.

functional_suitability.note: Assay coverage is substantial, but the central simulation does not validate realized FDR before design use.

reliability.note: Version and failure-mode guidance is strong; no realized-FDR stop/iterate response is given.

performance_context.note: The primary PROPER example is material work without a reduced documented smoke test.

agent_usability.note: Decision routing and runnable examples are clear, but the critical FDR validation action is absent.

human_usability.note: Plain-language explanation of what to do after Actual FDR exceeds target is missing.

security.note: No secrets or unsafe command construction were found; rnapower input guards remain prose-only.

maintainability.note: The two source examples parse and the FDR correction is localized.

agent_specific.note: Named handoffs and seed documentation are good; no explicit failure escape hatch exists for an FDR-invalid design.

recommendations.title: Make realized FDR an executable design-acceptance rule
recommendations.problem: Both fresh simulations show that a nominal 0.05 setting can produce Actual FDR above 0.05, while the skill permits treating marginal power as target-FDR power.
recommendations.root_cause: The workflow passes a targetFDR setting into PROPER but never checks summaryPower's realized Actual FDR before accepting or reporting a design.
recommendations.fix: Immediately after summaryPower, require Actual FDR <= predefined target with a stated Monte Carlo tolerance before reporting or selecting a replicate count. If it fails, mark the candidate invalid, increase nsims for stability, and refit the dispersion/effect model or revise the DE method. Apply the same rule to pseudobulk simulations.

recommendations.title: Ship a closed-form input preflight guard
recommendations.problem: RNASeqPower accepts invalid alpha and effect values with plausible numeric outputs.
recommendations.root_cause: The documented closed-form route forwards unchecked user inputs to rnapower, whose numeric return value does not enforce the workflow's scientific input domain.
recommendations.fix: Add a runnable validator for finite values, alpha/power in (0,1), positive depth/CV/n, and a positive non-unit fold change before every rnapower call.
